editorial.overview_md: Stratton Mountain Resort is on Stratton Mountain in Stratton, Vermont, east of Manchester. It opened in December 1961. In the 1980s it became the first ski area to allow snowboarding and home to the first snowboard school, and it hosted the Burton U.S. Open Snowboarding Championships from 1985 to 2012. Stratton Mountain School, founded at the mountain in 1972, has produced 46 Olympic athletes. Alterra Mountain Company has owned Stratton since 2017, when it was formed through the purchase of Intrawest.
editorial.culture_md: In the 1960s a group of Austrian ski instructors, the Stratton Mountain Boys, started European style après ski at Stratton and became part of its marketing. Intrawest later built premium real estate at the base, including the Village Common and ski in, ski out homes. The resort community of Stratton Mountain spans the towns of Stratton (440 people in 2020) and Winhall (1,182). Stratton Mountain School tuition for 2023 to 2024 was $65,500 for boarders.

editorial.overview_md: Sugar Bowl sits on Donner Pass near Norden, California, about 46 miles west of Reno on I 80. It opened on December 15, 1939. Austrian champion Hannes Schroll founded it with individual investors, and Walt Disney became a shareholder. It was the first ski area in California with a chairlift and the first on the West Coast with a gondola. Sugar Bowl is known for its history, advanced terrain and heavy snowfall, and it is one of the few privately owned resorts left in the Lake Tahoe area.
editorial.culture_md: Sugar Bowl is one of the closest ski areas to the San Francisco Bay Area, and many trails carry San Francisco names such as Nob Hill and Market Street. In its early years Hollywood guests came, and wearing suit jackets to dinner was the norm. Skiers from Sacramento and San Francisco skied the area before the resort opened, at the Klein ski school founded in 1936.

editorial.overview_md: Sugarbush Resort sits in the Mad River Valley in Warren, Vermont, and is one of the largest ski resorts in New England. It has two mountain areas, Lincoln Peak and Mount Ellen, joined by the Slide Brook Express chairlift over the expert Slide Brook Basin. Its 2,600 foot vertical drop is the second largest in Vermont after Killington. Damon and Sara Gadd and Jack Murphy opened it on Christmas Day 1958. Alterra Mountain Company bought Sugarbush in November 2019. It shares the valley with Mad River Glen in the Central Vermont cluster.
editorial.culture_md: The Mad River Valley towns of Warren (1,977 people in 2020), Waitsfield (1,844) and Fayston (1,364) surround the resort. Waitsfield's economy is largely supported by Sugarbush and Mad River Glen, along with its restaurants and lodging. Green Mountain Valley School trains racers on the Inverness slopes at Mount Ellen. Lincoln Peak Village, finished in 2010, added the Claybrook luxury condominiums and a Schoolhouse for children's programs.

editorial.overview_md: Sugarloaf is a ski resort on Sugarloaf Mountain in Carrabassett Valley, western Maine. It is the second largest ski resort east of the Mississippi by skiable area, has the highest peak elevation of any New England ski resort, and offers the only lift served skiing above treeline in the Northeast. The Sugarloaf Mountain Ski Club cut the first trail in 1950. Boyne Resorts has managed Sugarloaf since 2007 and bought the resort in March 2018. Carrabassett Valley Academy, at the base, counts 12 Olympians among its alumni.
editorial.culture_md: Carrabassett Valley is a town of 673 people (2020 census) that incorporated in 1971 and played a large role in Sugarloaf's development. Kingfield, population 960, is the principal gateway to the resort and home of the Ski Museum of Maine. Most trails carry logging terms as a tribute to Maine's logging history. Carrabassett Valley Academy draws students from Japan, Korea, Europe, Australia, New Zealand and South Africa.

editorial.overview_md: Sun Valley is the ski resort on Bald Mountain, or Baldy, next to Ketchum in Idaho's Wood River Valley. Union Pacific chairman W. Averell Harriman opened it in 1936 as the first destination winter resort in the U.S., and Baldy opened for lift served skiing in 1939 to 1940. The mountain has a 9,150 foot summit and 3,400 feet of vertical, with long runs at a steady pitch. The Holding family owns the resort, which Earl Holding bought in 1977.
editorial.culture_md: Sun Valley has been a seasonal home to the rich and famous since Ernest Hemingway brought it to public attention in the late 1930s. Harriman invited Hollywood celebrities to promote the resort, and Hemingway later moved to Ketchum. Ketchum had 3,555 residents in 2020, and Sun Valley had 1,783, with 66.6 percent of its housing units vacant. The area hosts the Sun Valley Music Festival, the Sun Valley Film Festival and Ketchum's Wagon Days each Labor Day weekend.

editorial.overview_md: Sunday River is a ski resort in Newry, Maine, and one of the state's largest and most visited. It has 139 trails across eight interconnected peaks, and its 2,340 foot vertical drop is the second largest in Maine after Sugarloaf. Boyne Resorts has operated it since American Skiing Company sold it with Sugarloaf in 2007, and Boyne bought its leased New England areas in 2018. Gould Academy athletes from nearby Bethel spend winter mornings training at Sunday River. It hosted the NCAA skiing championships in 1976, 1999 and 2009.
editorial.culture_md: Newry is a resort town of 411 year round residents (2020 census) with a proportionately large winter population. Bethel, population 2,504, was a fashionable summer resort between the Civil War and World War I and is home to Gould Academy. Local traditions include Santa Sunday, a charity ski in Santa suits held since 2000, and the Bust 'N' Burn mogul contest, revived in 2024.

editorial.overview_md: Taos Ski Valley is a village and ski resort in Taos County, New Mexico. Ernie and Rhoda Blake founded it in 1955, and they lived in an eleven foot camper before any lodge was finished. In 2006, 51 percent of its 110 trails were rated advanced or expert. Taos banned snowboarding until March 2008. Its Kachina lift reaches 12,481 feet. The Blake family sold Taos Ski Valley, Inc. to conservationist Louis Bacon in December 2013.
editorial.culture_md: Tourism is the village's main industry. In the 2011 to 2012 season the ski company employed about 700 people in winter, and about $47 million is spent in the village economy in an average year. The village had 77 residents in 2020. The town of Taos has a long reputation as an artist colony and counterculture haven next to Taos Pueblo, a UNESCO World Heritage Site. A fare free bus runs seasonally from Taos to the ski valley.

editorial.overview_md: Telluride Ski Resort spans the historic town of Telluride and the newer alpine community of Mountain Village in the San Juan Mountains of southwest Colorado. It has over 2,000 skiable acres. Telluride is known for its advanced terrain, and over half its runs are beginner or intermediate. Joe Zoline founded the ski area, which started in the 1970 to 1971 season. A free gondola links Telluride and Mountain Village. Chuck Horning, a Newport Beach real estate investor, took over ownership in February 2004.
editorial.culture_md: Telluride is a former silver mining camp in a box canyon, and its historic district is a National Historic Landmark. When the Pandora mine closed in 1978, skiing and tourism became the town's income. Young newcomers the locals called hippies replaced many mining families. Telluride has hosted the Bluegrass Festival and the Film Festival since 1974 and Mountainfilm since 1979. In the 1980s wealthy skiers flocked to the mountain all winter. Telluride had 2,607 residents in 2020 and Mountain Village had 1,264.

editorial.overview_md: The Highlands at Harbor Springs is a ski resort near Harbor Springs in northern Michigan, owned and operated by Boyne Resorts. It opened as Harbor Highlands in 1955, closed, and reopened under Boyne in 1963 as Boyne Highlands with the world's first triple chairlifts. It expanded into the North Peak area in 1995 and took its current name in December 2021. A high speed six passenger chairlift replaced three triple chairs in 2023. It is the sister resort of Boyne Mountain.
editorial.culture_md: Harbor Springs is a city and resort community of 1,274 people (2020 census) in Emmet County, known for historic summer resorts such as Wequetonsing. The Little Traverse Bay Bands of Odawa Indians have their tribal offices in the city. The golf series The Big Break X: Michigan was filmed at the resort.

editorial.overview_md: Timberline Lodge ski area sits on the south face of Mount Hood, about 60 miles east of Portland, below the Works Progress Administration lodge that President Roosevelt dedicated in 1937. Most of its terrain lies below the lodge. It opened as Oregon's first destination ski resort with a portable rope tow, and its Magic Mile chairlift, built in 1938, was then the longest chairlift in existence. The lodge is publicly owned and privately operated; Richard Kohnstamm took over in 1955, and his family still manages the resort.
editorial.culture_md: Timberline Lodge is a National Historic Landmark that draws two million visitors a year, and local artisans built and furnished it during the Great Depression. It served as the exterior of the Overlook Hotel in The Shining. Government Camp, the de facto ski town of Mount Hood, had 179 residents in 2020. The Golden Rose Ski Classic, run here since 1936 as part of the Portland Rose Festival, is the oldest known organized ski race in America.

editorial.overview_md: The Palmer Snowfield on Mount Hood's south slope gives Timberline lift served skiing through the summer. The Palmer chairlift, built in 1983, climbs to 8,500 feet and runs from spring to early fall when conditions allow. Summer skiing and race camps began at Timberline in 1956. Dozens of summer camps enroll thousands of athletes, and a busy midweek day can see 1,500 riders. Ski racing camps are the most popular, followed by snowboard and freeski camps. The season usually ends in August or September.
editorial.culture_md: Summer at Timberline centers on week long camps, with snow sessions in the morning and rafting, biking, hiking or trampoline in the afternoon. Lifts are busiest Monday through Friday in summer because of the camps. Mount Hood Summer Ski Camps have hosted campers since the 1970s. The snowfield is shrinking each year, and salting to extend the season adds pollution to the Salmon River.

editorial.overview_md: Vail Ski Resort sits above the town of Vail in Eagle County, Colorado, 97 miles west of Denver on I 70. At 5,289 acres it is the third largest single mountain ski resort in the U.S., with the Front Side, the Back Bowls and Blue Sky Basin. Vail opened in late 1962, founded by Pete Seibert and local rancher Earl Eaton. Vail Resorts owns and operates it along with nearby Beaver Creek, Breckenridge and Keystone. The company ranks Vail the second most visited mountain resort in the U.S. for the 2025/2026 season.
editorial.culture_md: Vail Village follows Bavarian village styles with pedestrian streets, and it was built when the resort opened. The town economy relies heavily on tourism. Vail had 4,835 residents in 2020, and 67.3 percent of its 7,300 housing units were vacant. The median house price is over $1 million, and the town faces a worker shortage because housing is insufficient. Starting in 2026/2027, every private lesson at Vail becomes Vail Resorts' Epic Ascent product, with concierge support and gear rental.

editorial.overview_md: Waterville Valley Resort is on Mount Tecumseh inside the planned resort community of Waterville Valley, New Hampshire, about 130 miles north of Boston off Interstate 93. A group led by Tom Corcoran opened it in 1966. It hosted World Cup alpine races from 1969 through most of the 1980s, and in 2024 it held the first dual moguls World Cup on American soil. Members of the Sununu family and area investors bought it in 2010, and it remains independent. Snowmaking covers about 100 percent of its terrain.
editorial.culture_md: Waterville Valley is a resort town of 508 people (2020 census) that draws winter visitors for alpine and cross country skiing. The Black and Blue Trail Smashers, founded in 1934, is one of the oldest ski clubs in the country and the home club of 2010 Olympic moguls champion Hannah Kearney. Waterville Valley Academy, founded in 1972, has around 160 students. The resort built New Hampshire's first terrain park.

editorial.overview_md: Whiteface ski area sits on the east slope of Whiteface Mountain in the town of Wilmington, New York, among the Adirondack High Peaks. It opened in 1960 and is run by the Olympic Regional Development Authority. Whiteface hosted all six alpine events of the 1980 Winter Olympics and alpine skiing at the 2023 Winter World University Games. Its hike to terrain, The Slides, gives it the greatest continuous vertical drop in eastern North America at 3,430 feet. Lake Placid, host of the 1932 and 1980 Winter Olympics, lies nearby.
editorial.culture_md: Wilmington is a town of 1,139 people (2020) inside the Adirondack Park, and its hamlet is a resort and skiing center. Tourism grew there early in the twentieth century, and Santa's Workshop, one of the first American theme parks for children, sits on the Whiteface highway. Lake Placid, a village of 2,205 people (2020 census), became internationally known for the 1932 and 1980 Winter Olympics.

editorial.overview_md: Whitefish Mountain Resort sits on Big Mountain in northwest Montana, west of Glacier National Park, 4 miles from the town of Whitefish and 21 miles north of Kalispell. Winter Sports, Inc. formed in 1947 as a public company of community shareholders to open Big Mountain. The resort hosted the U.S. Alpine Championships in 1949, and Olympic champion Tommy Moe learned to ski and race here. Big Mountain took its current name after billionaire Bill Foley became majority shareholder of Winter Sports, Inc. It has 14 lifts.
editorial.culture_md: Local people donated labor to build the resort, clearing slopes and helping push through the mountain road. Whitefish had 7,751 residents in 2020 and is known for environmentalism and protected trails. Its events include the Whitefish Winter Carnival, with a parade and a plunge into Whitefish Lake, and the Under the Big Sky Music Festival. Amtrak's Empire Builder stops in Whitefish on its Chicago to Seattle and Portland route.

editorial.overview_md: Whitetail Resort is on Two Top Mountain in the Bear Pond Mountains of Pennsylvania, between Mercersburg and Clear Spring, Maryland. It opened in 1991, joined Snow Time, Inc. a few years later, passed to Peak Resorts in 2018 and to Vail Resorts in 2019. Its trails are laid out so each ability level has its own area and lift, a design that won Snow Country Magazine's 1992 Best Overall Resort Design Award. Seasons usually run 80 to 100 days.
editorial.culture_md: Whitetail serves the Baltimore Washington metropolitan area, 89 miles from Washington, D.C., and 92 miles from Baltimore. It gets crowded on weekends and holidays and is quieter on weekdays. Mercersburg, a borough 7 miles north of the resort, had 1,561 people in 2010. Vail says its Mid Atlantic ski areas offer local options and easy overnight weekend trips.

editorial.overview_md: Wildcat Mountain is a ski area in Pinkham Notch near Jackson, New Hampshire, with a view of Mount Washington. Its 2,112 foot vertical drop is the second largest in New Hampshire, and its Polecat trail is the longest in the state. Wildcat opened the first gondola in North America in 1958, and the Civilian Conservation Corps cut its original racing trail in 1933. More than 200 inches of snow a year usually keep it open from mid November to early May. Vail Resorts bought it with Attitash in 2019.
editorial.culture_md: Jackson is a town of 1,028 people (2020 census) and a resort area in the White Mountains, where painters arrived from 1847 and grand hotels followed the railroad. It is known for Jackson Falls and its 100 kilometer cross country ski trail system. The ungroomed Wildcat Valley Trail runs from Wildcat's summit down to the village. In winter, skiers from the valley resorts spend their evenings in North Conway.

editorial.overview_md: Wilmot Mountain is a ski area in Kenosha County, Wisconsin, just north of the Illinois border, 55 miles north of Chicago and 40 miles from Milwaukee. Walter Stopa founded it in 1938, and his family ran it until Vail Resorts bought it in 2016 and spent about $13 million on renovations that year. It calls itself the Matterhorn of the Midwest and has about 200 feet of vertical, wide open slopes and night skiing on the whole hill.
editorial.culture_md: Wilmot's ski and snowboard school has over 300 certified instructors and a full children's program. The Chicago Metropolitan Ski Council holds slalom and giant slalom races here eight days each season, and the resort runs weekly evening race training. Its longest run, State Line, parallels the Illinois and Wisconsin border. Vail lists Chicago among the metro markets its Midwest ski areas draw from.

editorial.overview_md: Winter Park Resort sits in Grand County, Colorado, just off U.S. Highway 40, about a ninety minute drive from Denver. It opened for the 1939 to 1940 season. The City and County of Denver owned and ran it until 2002 and still owns it, and Alterra Mountain Company manages it. Its Mary Jane area, opened in 1975, has a separate base and is known for moguls, trees and harder terrain. The resort has 23 lifts and is home to the National Sports Center for the Disabled, one of the world's largest and oldest disabled skiing programs.
editorial.culture_md: For nearly 70 years many Denver residents rode the Ski Train to the base through the Moffat Tunnel, and Amtrak's Winter Park Express now runs seasonal ski trains. The town of Winter Park had 1,033 permanent residents in 2020, and 81.3 percent of its housing units were vacant, so the seasonal population is much higher. Nearby Fraser, a town of 1,400, has grown with new condominiums. The Lift bus serves the town, and Bustang links it to Denver.

editorial.overview_md: The Yellowstone Club is a private residential club, ski resort and golf resort in Madison County, Montana, just west of Big Sky. Most of its runs are on Pioneer Mountain, with a 9,859 foot summit, and its lifts tie into Big Sky Resort along a five mile shared border. Developer Tim Blixseth assembled the land. Out of bankruptcy in June 2009, CrossHarbor Capital Partners, led by club member Sam Byrne, bought the club for $115 million.
editorial.culture_md: The club is rated among the top 10 lifestyle estates in the world. By late 2014 it had more than 500 member households, and members have included Bill Gates and Mark Zuckerberg. Almost 650 people work at the club in peak season. Big Sky lies 45 miles by road from Bozeman.
